Calculate observed demographic event rates

Source: R/calculate_rates.R
calculate_rates.Rd

Calculate age-specific mortality, fertility, union formation, dissolution, cohabitation conversion, and group transition rates from simulated data by time intervals. Rates can be stratified across a variety of dimensions.

Usage

calculate_mortality_rates(
  population,
  time_breaks,
  age_breaks,
  by = NULL,
  conf_level = NULL,
  use_detailed_previous_union = TRUE
)

calculate_fertility_rates(
  population,
  time_breaks,
  age_breaks,
  by = NULL,
  parity_breaks = NULL,
  unrealized = FALSE,
  conf_level = NULL,
  use_detailed_previous_union = TRUE
)

calculate_union_rates(
  population,
  time_breaks,
  age_breaks,
  dur_breaks = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  conf_level = NULL,
  use_detailed_previous_union = TRUE
)

calculate_marriage_rates(
  population,
  time_breaks,
  age_breaks,
  by = NULL,
  conf_level = NULL,
  use_detailed_previous_union = TRUE
)

calculate_dissolution_rates(
  population,
  time_breaks,
  dur_breaks,
  by = NULL,
  conf_level = NULL
)

calculate_cohab_convert_rate(
  population,
  time_breaks,
  dur_breaks = NULL,
  age_breaks = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  conf_level = NULL
)

calculate_transition_rates(
  population,
  time_breaks,
  age_breaks = NULL,
  dur_breaks = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  conf_level = NULL,
  use_detailed_previous_union = TRUE,
  group = NULL
)

Arguments

population

A hammel_population object returned from run_simulation().

time_breaks

Strictly increasing finite calendar boundaries in years or fractions of years that define the time intervals of the Lexis surface.

age_breaks

Strictly increasing nonnegative age boundaries in years or fractions of years that define the age intervals of the Lexis surface. If the last boundary is finite, an open-ended age interval extended to Inf is added. Required for mortality, fertility, and marriage. Cohabitation conversion and group transitions require exactly one of age_breaks and dur_breaks. Union formation can take both (see details below).

by

Character vector of variables to stratify rates across. Defaults to NULL for no stratification. Accepted stratification variables differ by calculator; see the sections below.

conf_level

NULL (default) to omit confidence intervals, or a finite numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1 indicating the level of confidence to use for rate confidence intervals. Adds conf_low and conf_high from two-sided exact stats::poisson.test() intervals for observed event counts over exposure. Bounds are NA at zero exposure. For fertility, these describe the observed rate, not the unrealized-adjusted rate.

use_detailed_previous_union

Logical value that indicates whether stratification by "previous_union" will use "separated" and "widowed" or a combined "dissolved" category.

parity_breaks

For fertility only: NULL to pool parities, or strictly increasing nonnegative integer boundaries starting at zero that define categories for stratifying by parity.

unrealized

For fertility only: logical, default FALSE. When TRUE, adds a column for rate_fertility_adjusted that gives the fertility rate when unrealized births (counted births that could not be realized because their fertility cell had members but no eligible women).

dur_breaks

Strictly increasing nonnegative duration boundaries in years or fractions of years that define the duration intervals of the Lexis surface. If the last boundary is finite, an open-ended duration interval extended to Inf is added. Required for union dissolution; optional for union formation; an alternative to age for cohabitation conversion and group transitions.

group

For group transitions only. The declared group dimension whose transitions are counted. NULL (default) means the only declared dimension and will only work when one group is defined.

Value

A tibble containing calendar bands, age or duration bands where applicable, requested strata, event counts, exposure, and the observed rate. Rates are NA at zero exposure; zero events with positive exposure give zero. Confidence limits are included only when requested. Person-based exposure uses person_years (woman-years for fertility); union-based exposure uses union_years. Each calculator's section specifies its count/rate columns, and additional output.

Details

Rates are calculated by counting person-years and events within a given Lexis triangle from a Lexis surface. Some rates allow for either age_breaks or dur_breaks but one must always be provided. time_breaks are also always required but users can specify a single time interval for the entire simulation.

All breaks defined by the function use half-open intervals that are inclusive at the lower bound and exclusive at the upper bound.

For more details on each rate, see below.

Choosing a calculator

CalculatorEventsExposure
MortalityDeathsPerson-years alive
FertilityMaternal birthsWoman-years alive
Union formationPartnership startsUnpartnered person-years
MarriageMarriage starts and conversionsNonmarried person-years
DissolutionDissolutionsUnion-years
Cohabitation conversionConversionsCohabitation union-years
Group transitionsDirected group movesPerson-years in origin category

Stratifying with by

The values by accepts in each calculator. Group means the name of a declared group dimension, such as "race" or "region".

Person-level rates count events and exposure for individuals:

FunctionGroupSexunion_typeprevious_union
calculate_mortality_rates()YesAlwaysYesYes
calculate_fertility_rates()YesWomenYesYes
calculate_union_rates()YesAlwaysYesYes (a)
calculate_marriage_rates()YesAlwaysNoYes
calculate_transition_rates()Yes (b)YesYesYes

Union-level rates count events and exposure for unions:

FunctionGroupunion_typeprevious_union
calculate_dissolution_rates()Yes (c)YesNo
calculate_cohab_convert_rate()Yes (c)NoNo

Always: results are always split by sex, so sex is not a by value. Women: fertility is reported for women only.

(a) Supplying dur_breaks adds previous_union automatically.

(b) Other declared dimensions only, not the one whose transitions are counted (the group argument).

(c) The partners' groups: "<dim>_w" for the wife's current category, "<dim>_h" for the husband's, or both for the couple's combination, such as c("race_w", "race_h"). A bare dimension name is ambiguous for a union.

(d)

Mortality

Use calculate_mortality_rates(): Reports deaths per person-year lived.

Fertility

Use calculate_fertility_rates(): Reports maternal births per woman-year, including time excluded by minimum birth spacing. Only female rows are returned. Current parity is reconstructed from all recorded maternal births, including pre-window births and deceased children. Setting unrealized = TRUE will calculate a separate rate_fertility_adjusted column that calculates fertility rates as if unrealized births were realized.

Union formation

Use calculate_union_rates(): Reports union starts (both marriage and cohabitation) per unpartnered person-year lived. Marriages that occur because of the conversion of a cohabitation are not counted as events in this function. To calculate cohabitation and direct marriage separately, use by = "union_type.

The age_breaks argument is always required for this function, but dur_breaks can also be used when stratified by previous_union to get duration-based rates for union formation since the previous marriage for individuals who have been previously married.

Marriage

Use calculate_marriage_rates(): Reports direct marriages and conversions to marriage from cohabitation over nonmarried person-years. Unpartnered and cohabiting time both contribute exposure. Married time contributes none.

Dissolution

Use calculate_dissolution_rates(): Reports union dissolutions over union-years lived. To calculate dissolution separately by marriage and cohabitation, use by = "union_type".

Dissolution can only be calculated using dur_breaks where duration is measured since the formation of the current union.

Cohabitation conversion

Use calculate_cohab_convert_rate(): Reports conversions from cohabitation to marriage over cohabitation union-years.

Group transitions

use calculate_transition_rates(): Reports state transitions from origin to destination category per person-years lived in origin category.

When more than one group is in use in a simulation, the group argument must be used to specify which group transition rates are desired. Transition rates can be stratified by other groups besides the focal group.

Transition rates can be defined by age_breaks or dur_breaks. If dur_breaks is used, The duration for the first transition is equivalent to age.

See also

calculate_population_size(), calculate_tfr(), calculate_patfr(), calculate_life_table()

Examples


# run a simulation
pop_start <- generate_uniform_population(1000, end_time = 0)
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(pop_start) |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility_union) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_union_formation("rate", rate = usa_2000_marriage)
pop_end <- run_simulation(model, 100)

calculate_mortality_rates(
  pop_end,
  time_breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
  age_breaks = c(0, 1, seq(5, 100, 5))
)
#> # A tibble: 220 × 8
#>    time_start time_end sex   age_start age_end person_years deaths
#>         <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>     <dbl>   <dbl>        <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1          0       20 m             0       1         129.      2
#>  2         20       40 m             0       1         108.      1
#>  3         40       60 m             0       1         120.      1
#>  4         60       80 m             0       1         121.      2
#>  5         80      100 m             0       1         111.      1
#>  6          0       20 m             1       5         541.      0
#>  7         20       40 m             1       5         425.      0
#>  8         40       60 m             1       5         484.      0
#>  9         60       80 m             1       5         469.      0
#> 10         80      100 m             1       5         459.      0
#> # ℹ 210 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: rate_mortality <dbl>

calculate_fertility_rates(
  pop_end,
  time_breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
  age_breaks = seq(15, 40, 5),
  by = "union_type"
)
#> # A tibble: 60 × 9
#>    time_start time_end sex   age_start age_end union_type  person_years births
#>         <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>              <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1          0       20 f            15      20 unpartnered         605.     15
#>  2         20       40 f            15      20 unpartnered         517.     17
#>  3         40       60 f            15      20 unpartnered         485.     18
#>  4         60       80 f            15      20 unpartnered         523.     21
#>  5         80      100 f            15      20 unpartnered         512.     16
#>  6          0       20 f            20      25 unpartnered         513.     38
#>  7         20       40 f            20      25 unpartnered         393.     24
#>  8         40       60 f            20      25 unpartnered         355.     26
#>  9         60       80 f            20      25 unpartnered         397.     28
#> 10         80      100 f            20      25 unpartnered         452.     29
#> # ℹ 50 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: rate_fertility <dbl>
